papers.title: Cardiac cobaltism: a rare complication after bilateral metal-on-metal total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: This is one of the first documented cases of metal-on-metal (MoM) total hip arthroplasty cobalt cardiac toxicity that has led to patient death. A 69-year-old female presented to our institution with cardiac failure secondary to cobalt toxicity resulting from bilateral MoM total hip arthroplasty. Her presenting metal ion levels were a cobalt level of 199 ppb and a chromium level of 77 ppb. She underwent bilateral femoral revisions to remove the source of cobalt. On postoperative day 7, the patient sustained a cerebral infarct and eventually expired because of the insult. This case represents one of the first documented fatalities related to MoM cobalt cardiac toxicity.

summary_en.motivation: To document a fatal case of cobalt cardiac toxicity following bilateral metal-on-metal total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: Clinical case report with serum metal ion measurement and patient history.
summary_en.result: The patient died from cerebral infarct after revision surgery despite removal of the cobalt source.
summary_en.validation: Single clinical case observation with laboratory confirmation.

summary_en.motivation: To develop an eco-friendly nanomaterial for mosquito control using plant-mediated synthesis.
summary_en.method: Silver nanoparticles were biofabricated using Clerodendrum chinense extract and characterized.
summary_en.result: The nanoparticles showed high larvicidal activity against mosquitoes with low toxicity to non-target organisms.
summary_en.validation: Laboratory bioassays confirmed mosquitocidal efficacy and acute toxicity to aquatic organisms.
